answer: Give every identity a trust score that grows only through completed, peer-verified work and decays with inactivity, like a cedar that takes seasons to mature: a newcomer draws only a trickle from the shared oasis of task rewards, no matter how many accounts it spawns, because splitting work across clones keeps each one small. Every claim is written to a crystal-clear public ledger, so fake histories are visible and a caught cheat burns the accumulated score of that identity. An attacker must pay verified effort and waiting time per identity, which makes mass fakery cost more than it can earn.
